 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The 2026-27 NBA season is here! Check out our team previews , including power rankings, best- and worst-case scenarios, and fantasy advice. 
 ATLANTA HAWKS
 2025-26 finish 
 Record: 46-36 (6th in the East, lost 4-2 in first round to Knicks)
 Offseason moves 
 Draft: Kingston Flemings (No. 8), Zuby Ejiofor (No. 23), Henri Veesaar (No. 52)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Signings: CJ McCollum (1 year, $21 million extension), Jock Landale (re-signed for 1 year, $14 million)
 Trades: Aaron Wiggins (from Thunder), Lu Dort (from Thunder), Dorian Finney-Smith (from Hornets)
 Key departures: Zaccharie Risacher (traded to Mavericks), Jonathan Kuminga (signed with Timberwolves)
 Current roster 
 Can Jalen Johnson carry the Hawks roster to new heights? (Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images)
 (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS) Preseason Power Rankings: No. 15 
 What's exciting: The Hawks added enough wings and bigs that some absences in the starting lineup shouldn't wreck the rotation. Dort provides another lockdown defender next to Dyson Daniels. Wiggins is another wing scorer like Nickeil Alexander-Walker. Flemings can support McCollum at point guard. Onyeka Okongwu and Jalen Johnson could both take another leap forward this year, and they now have Ejiofor and Jock Landale to support them in the frontcourt. With so much talented depth, head coach Quin Snyder has to be enjoying thinking up all the lineup possibilities.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What's concerning: This team is built to rack up regular-season wins, but what happens when the first action gets snuffed out? That could hold them back from becoming true contenders. McCollum scored 0.82 points per isolation with the Hawks last season, per Synergy. NAW? 0.85. Johnson? 0.78. All three of them finished below the 50th percentile. Every close game doesn't require a one-on-one bucket to win, but it sure is necessary come playoff time. — Kevin O'Connor  
 Preseason Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up ahead of 2026-27 
 Preseason takeaways
 The task for the Hawks is going to be figuring out how to build on their post All-Star break run from last season. My eyes go directly to Jalen Johnson and what another leap looks like. There is a poise and composure to his game in the half-court. As important as his drives have been, watching him work to get to his spots feels like the next evolution. Developing confidence in that in-between game, being willing to mix in pull-up 3s. It will be key for him to draw more attention from defenses, but he'll have to be able to score even when they don't bring help and force the defense's hand. Also, you can yell at me about spacing, but go watch Lu Dort and Dyson Daniels play defense at the same time. — Steve Jones 
 Fantasy watch 
 I'm on the fence about Jalen Johnson as a first-round pick. The counting stats look great (22.5/10.3/7.9 last year), but I think I've been underestimating CJ McCollum's impact for 9-cat specifically. In 36 games without CJ, Johnson was 9th in per-game value; 36 games with him, 34th. Not bad, but that's a two-round drop-off. Suffice it to say, the second round is probably more appropriate. — Dan Titus

 Best case, worst case 
 Best case: No. 3 seed 
 The defense remains chaotic in the best way, thus fueling an elite transition attack. Half-court growth from Johnson makes him more of a pressure point, making him and his supporting cast more difficult to deal with. A high-octane, egalitarian offense paired with a turnover-forcing defense could absolutely churn out 50 wins.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement They did win at a 53-win pace (28-15 from 1/9 onward) following the Trae Young trade, after all.
 Worst case: Play-In Tournament 
 The East is tough, which could put them in the 7-10 range by default. Beyond that, I do wonder what the offense looks like if teams continue to land on switching to flatten them out. Their ability to force turnovers helped offset some of the size (and early season rebounding) issues they had; any slippage in that area could also lower their floor. — Nekias Duncan
